messages.text: England Wheelchair rout Australia to reach World Cup final

metadata.summary: England Wheelchair scored a record points total against rival Australia to rout their opponents 86-18 and reach their fifth successive Rugby League World Cup final.
metadata.content: Rugby League World Cup: England Wheelchair score record points total against home nation Australia to reach final | Rugby League News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Rugby League World Cup: England Wheelchair score record points total against home nation Australia to reach final England Wheelchair beat Australia 86-18 to reach fifth successive Rugby League World Cup final; Rob Hawkins led the charge for his side with a stunning 30-point performance; England face France in World Cup final in Wollongong on Friday Noah Langford Sports Journalist Tuesday 10 November 2026 11:15, UK Image: Mason Billington celebrates scoring a try England Wheelchair scored a record points total against rival Australia to rout their opponents 86-18 and reach their fifth successive Rugby League World Cup final. The game was all but over at half-time as England held a 40-6 lead, with Rob Hawkins leading the charge for his side with a stunning 30-point performance in his side's dominant victory. The win means the defending World Cup champions will face France in the final in Wollongong on Friday, with a chance to claim their third World Cup title. messages.text: Tough-tackling Schlager proves his worth for Forest

metadata.summary: Xaver Schlager has been quietly impressive for Nottingham Forest this season but what was missing was that big moment. It came in the 3-1 win over Manchester City on Saturday when he dispossessed Elliot Anderson for Liam Delap's first goal.
metadata.content: Xaver Schlager at Nottingham Forest: Tough-tackling replacement for Elliot Anderson proves his worth to new club | Football News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Analysis Xaver Schlager at Nottingham Forest: Tough-tackling replacement for Elliot Anderson proves his worth to new club Xaver Schlager has made more tackles than any other player in the Premier League and it helped Nottingham Forest beat Manchester City. With insight from his coaches past and present, Adam Bate examines why the unsung Austrian is quietly impressive... Adam Bate Football Features Writer @ghostgoal Tuesday 10 November 2026 10:49, UK Image: Xaver Schlager is an underrated player but he enjoyed a big moment in Nottingham Forest's win over Manchester City Xaver Schlager has been quietly impressive for Nottingham Forest this season but what was missing was that big moment. It came in the 3-1 win over Manchester City on Saturday when he dispossessed Elliot Anderson for Liam Delap's first goal. The free transfer from Leipzig nipped in ahead of the £116m man that he has replaced in Forest's midfield and set Delap on the way to doubling the lead. Schlager is no Anderson but he has his own qualities and they made the difference at the weekend. "It was a top team performance and it was a top performance by Xaver Schlager," said Forest boss Oliver Glasner in the press conference afterwards. messages.text: England Lions hit record score as McKinney runs riot

metadata.summary: England Lions thumped their highest List A score of all time - and the fifth best by any side - as they piled on 487-5 from 50 overs against West Indies A in the second unofficial ODI in St Kitts.
metadata.content: England Lions hit their highest List A cricket score of 487-5 as Durham's Ben McKinney smashes 145 from 65 balls | Cricket News | Sky Sports Skip to main content England Lions hit their highest List A cricket score of 487-5 as Durham's Ben McKinney smashes 145 from 65 balls Durham opener Ben McKinney smashes 15 fours and 10 sixes in his eye-catching century as England Lions make it five wins from five on West Indies tour; James Rew also scores a ton as Lions eclipse the Ben Duckett-inspired 425-1 the Lions amassed against Sri Lanka A in Canterbury in 2016 Tuesday 10 November 2026 11:23, UK Image: Durham opener Ben McKinney smashed 15 fours and 10 sixes in his century as England Lions made it five wins from five on their West Indies tour England Lions thumped their highest List A score of all time - and the fifth best by any side - as they piled on 487-5 from 50 overs against West Indies A in the second unofficial ODI in St Kitts. The total, in which Durham opener Ben McKinney looted 145 from 65 deliveries - reaching his century from just 43 balls - and James Rew scored 107 not out from 56, eclipsed the 425-1 the Lions racked up against Sri Lanka A at Canterbury a decade ago. In that match, current England Test and ODI opener Ben Duckett plundered 220 not out from 131 balls and Kent's Daniel Bell-Drummond 171 from 139 after Dawid Malan had fallen for 23. metadata.summary: Michael Carrick's position as Manchester United head coach is looking increasingly in doubt, with Mauricio Pochettino open to a discussion with Man Utd if he were approached by the club.
metadata.content: Michael Carrick future: Man Utd head coach position increasingly in doubt with Mauricio Pochettino open to talks | Football News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Update Michael Carrick future: Man Utd head coach position increasingly in doubt with Mauricio Pochettino open to talks Man Utd head coach Michael Carrick's position under increasing threat, but no final decision; Sky Sports News understands Mauricio Pochettino would be open to a discussion with Man Utd if he approached by club; it is thought the cost of buying him out of his USA contract is around £7m Tuesday 10 November 2026 11:00, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Sky Sports News provides an update on Michael Carrick's future at Manchester United Michael Carrick's position as Manchester United head coach is looking increasingly in doubt, with Mauricio Pochettino open to a discussion with Man Utd if he were approached by the club. Sky Sports News has been told that, as yet, no final decision has been taken on Carrick's Old Trafford future. With Pochettino open to Man Utd talks, it is thought the cost of buying him out of his contract with his current job as USA head coach would be around £7m. The former Argentina defender recently extended his deal with the USA until 2030 and is preparing to face Haiti in the Nations League quarter-finals.
